Hi Joe — great conversation today. Thanks for walking through the intended workflows and the top-line success objective (reduce triage time for intake by 40%). As promised, here’s a concise post-call recap and a proposed evaluation approach that leans on measurable evidence rather than subjective checks.

Summary of ask
- Primary goal: Improve intake triage accuracy and speed; target end-user latency requirement is < 300ms P95 for in-app calls.
- Success gate: demonstrated reduction in manual triage labor by 40% within trial scope and model-level hallucination <= 2% on sampled clinical flows.

Proposed evidence-driven sprint charter (2-week cadence)
1) Week 1 — Shadow & offline baseline
   - Shadow mode for 48 hours on a 5% traffic sample (non-blocking) to capture real inputs and outputs.
   - In parallel, run offline evals on historical intake transcripts (500–1,000 examples) with human-labeled ground truth.
   - Deliverables: confusion matrix, hallucination examples catalog, initial latency profile.
2) Week 2 — Controlled A/B on synthetic workload + acceptance grading
   - Use the synthetic test harness (replicates peak token distribution) for stress runs across model variants and quant profiles.
   - Run a graded rubric on a curated 200-case test set with clinical annotations.
   - Deliverables: graded scorecard, cost-per-1000-token estimate, recommended model/config for rollout.

Evaluation methodology decisions (shadow vs offline)
- Why both: offline evals give controlled repeatability and quick iteration; shadow captures distributional shift and real-world failure modes (prefix-handling, prompt engineering effects). We recommend a hybrid: start with offline to establish baseline metrics, then shadow to validate generalization and surface rare failure modes.
- Sampling: prioritize high-impact intents (eligibility checks, insurance verification, intake triage) and include long-tail edge cases (hand-written notes, multi-language snippets).

Grading rubric (proposed quick version)
- Accuracy: binary match to human-labeled intent (weight 40%)
- Hallucination/incorrect content: rate per 100 responses (weight 25%)
- Latency: P95 measured on the shadow sample (weight 15%)
- Cost: tokens-per-session normalized to baseline (weight 10%)
- Safety/PII leakage checks: automated flagging + manual review (weight 10%)
Acceptance thresholds (preliminary)
- Weighted score >= 82% to pass
- Hallucination <= 2% on the curated clinical set
- P95 latency < 300ms on production-like VM/GPU config

Ownership & next steps (short list)
- Rishi: overall trial owner, primary contact for HelixCare (I’ll coordinate SSO and infra access).
- Ben: test harness + synthetic workload setup; will prepare the synthetic token distribution and load-generator.
- Priyom: contract/PO chase and trial billing questions (Priyom will loop procurement if needed).
- Karthik: success metrics + evaluation rubric finalization; will own the scorecard.

Immediate asks for HelixCare
1) Confirm the 5% shadow sample window and preferred dates (we’re tentatively proposing Aug 25–27 for initial shadow).
2) Share two representative historical transcripts (redacted) for offline labeling — prefer recent intake and one edge-case example.
3) Procurement point-of-contact for trial PO (if needed).

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft criteria spreadsheet and a simple network diagram showing where the shadow tap happens.

I’ll follow up with calendar invites and a short one-pager that maps the rubric to the deliverables noted above. Thoughts?
